# Results summary (auto-generated by the notebook)

- Customers: 7043, original columns: 21
- Training / testing customers: 5634 / 1409
- Overall churn rate: 26.5%

## EDA findings
- Churn distribution: only 26.5% of customers churned, so the data is imbalanced. A model that always says 'No churn' would still look accurate, which is why we also look at Recall and F1-score for the churn class.
- Gender: 'Female' customers churn the most (26.9%), 'Male' customers churn the least (26.2%), a gap of 0.8 percentage points.
- Gender: The difference is small (under 2 percentage points), so gender is not a strong factor for churn.
- Contract type: 'Month-to-month' customers churn the most (42.7%), 'Two year' customers churn the least (2.8%), a gap of 39.9 percentage points.
- Monthly charges: churned customers pay on average 74.44 per month versus 61.27 for customers who stayed (13.17 higher).
- Tenure: churned customers have a median tenure of 10 months compared with 38 months for customers who stayed. The churn rate is highest in the '0-12 months' group (47.4%) and lowest in the '49+ months' group (9.5%).
- Internet service: 'Fiber optic' customers churn the most (41.9%), 'No' customers churn the least (7.4%), a gap of 34.5 percentage points.
- Correlation: 'tenure' has the strongest linear relationship with churn (-0.35). A negative value means churn becomes less likely as the feature increases. Correlation only covers numeric columns and straight-line relationships, so the models in the next sections also use the categorical columns.

## Model comparison (test data)

| Model | Accuracy | Precision (Churn) | Recall (Churn) | F1-score (Churn) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic Regression | 0.7381 | 0.5043 | 0.7834 | 0.6136 |

## Conclusion
- Based on the F1-score for the churn class, Decision Tree performs better (0.623 vs 0.614).
- However, Logistic Regression has the higher recall (0.783), so it catches more churners, while Decision Tree gives a better balance between recall and precision.
